Goal: build the meeting-room booking HTTP server `server.mjs` (ES module, Node.js built-ins only, no npm install; Node v22) in /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23, plus `package.json`.

Read first: `.team/notes/INDEX.md`, then `.team/notes/spec.md` (the full, final user spec — implement every Server, API and Booking-rules line exactly) and `.team/notes/decisions.md` (file layout, data-file layout `{nextId, bookings}`, atomic save via temp+rename with rollback on failure, serialized mutations).

Key points (spec wins on any conflict):
- Startup order: validate PORT (only ASCII digits, <= 65535; unset/empty → 3000) → read DATA_FILE (unset/empty → bookings.json, relative to cwd; ENOENT → empty; other error or invalid layout → stderr `cannot read data file <name as given>\n`, exit 1) → listen on 127.0.0.1 (bind error → one stderr line, exit 1) → stdout exactly `listening on http://127.0.0.1:<actual port>\n` and nothing else ever on stdout.
- Never write the data file except on successful POST create / DELETE remove; never mkdir. Failed save → 500 `internal error`, memory and nextId unchanged. Any unexpected error → 500, server keeps running. Temp file must not be left behind on failure where avoidable, and the temp file must be in the same folder (so a missing folder fails the save).
- Always read the whole request body before replying (also for 413/415/404/405), counting received bytes for the 10000 limit (don't stop reading; discard).
- Routing byte-for-byte on raw path before first `?`; DELETE /api/bookings/<id> route covers any non-empty id without `/`; 405 for other methods on known paths (HEAD/OPTIONS included); 404 `not found` otherwise.
- Serve `public/index.html` at `GET /` (text/html; charset=utf-8) and `public/app.js` at `GET /app.js` (text/javascript; charset=utf-8), resolved relative to server.mjs (import.meta.url). The frontend section is writing those two files in parallel; you only serve them. Read them at startup or per request — your choice, but a missing file must not crash the server.
- All JSON replies: `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`; 204 has empty body.
- `package.json`: `{"name": ..., "type": "module", "scripts": {"start": "node server.mjs", "test": "node --test test/"}}` — no dependencies. (Testing section will write tests under `test/` later; you may add a quick smoke test of your own there as `test/server.smoke.test.mjs` if you like.)
- Where a spec line reads two ways, build the stricter reading and note it in your REPORT.
- Write a short note `.team/notes/backend-api.md` (and add a line to INDEX.md) describing: env vars, data file layout, how the server locates public/ files, and any exported helpers (if you export nothing, say so — running `node server.mjs` must start the server).

Skills for this job: none required (use your own judgement; no installs).

Gate for this mode: run `section-team:reviewer` on your changed files before you hand back. Pass = overall at least 9 and no item under 7; up to 3 fix rounds. Near-miss check: the testing section will later make near-miss copies of key functions in `.team/near-miss/`; the gate fails while any near-miss passes the tests.

Done means: `node server.mjs` works per spec, you manually verified startup errors, routing, all 10 booking rules, persistence across restart, concurrent overlapping POSTs, and save failure (DATA_FILE in a non-existent folder) with a quick script or curl; package.json exists; reviewer gate passed.

Other awake sections: frontend and docs were woken at the same time as you (no ids yet) — coordinate through notes; ask `main` if you must. Do not review other sections' work.

End with your REPORT block.

The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. 22:- Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. 23:- A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. 24:- `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. 25:- `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. 26:- `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. 27:- `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. 28:- `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). 29:- Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. - `node server.mjs` (or `npm start`) starts the server. `server.mjs` exports nothing; importing it starts the server.

- `PORT`: unset/empty means 3000. Only ASCII digits, value <= 65535, else one stderr line `invalid PORT: <value>`, exit 1.

- stdout: only `listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port>\n`. Unexpected request errors are logged to stderr as one line.

`{"nextId": <int >= 1>, "bookings": [{"id","room","title","date","start","end"}, ...]}`
Loading is strict: each booking needs exactly those 6 keys, a safe-integer id in 1..nextId-1, unique ids, valid
room/date/times, end > start, an already-trimmed title of 1-80 chars, and no two stored bookings may overlap.

  an in-process promise queue (overlap check + save inside the queue).

- `GET /` serves `public/index.html` (`text/html; charset=utf-8`), `GET /app.js` serves `public/app.js`

- ENOTDIR (a path component is a file) is not ENOENT, so it gives `cannot read data file`.
- HEAD on any known path gets 405 (no auto-HEAD for GET routes).
- Overlapping stored bookings in the data file count as an invalid layout.

entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.
